confidence: moderate — direction and magnitude are corroborated by sourced item text; the exact float is NOT independently reproducible from the permitted evidence tree (see limits)

what_the_leaf_is.quantity: per-event overheal on a healing event inside a coupled roster fight
what_the_leaf_is.identity: overheal = max(0, heal_amount - missing_health_of_target_at_event_time); applied = heal_amount - overheal
what_the_leaf_is.identity_source: docs/math-foundations.md Sec. 5, 'Shield absorption (survival walk)' row states the engine's clipping convention explicitly: `absorbed = min(shield, damage)`, `overkill = max(0, damage - absorbed)`, `absorbed + overkill = damage` (verdict EXACT). Overheal is the same clipping identity applied on the healing side; docs/math-foundations.md contains no separate overheal theorem.
what_the_leaf_is.event_schema_source: data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json — healing events carry {source, time, amount|raw, applied, factor, trigger_source} (e.g. scenario 'e9-e8-morellonomicon-grievous': {time 0.25, raw 277.8, applied 166.7, factor 0.6}), confirming heals are authored raw and then clipped/reduced.

independent_computation.step_1_algebra: Both readings of the diff are exhausted by the identity. (a) heal unchanged, target fuller: delta_overheal = -delta_missing_health = +14.1, i.e. the healed unit had exactly 14.1 less missing health at that timestamp. (b) heal changed, missing health unchanged: heal grew by 14.1, a factor 46.7/32.6 = 1.43252 (rounding-consistent band [1.4288, 1.4363]).
independent_computation.step_2_rule_out_mitigation_and_shred: Reading (b) as a mitigation/shred effect is impossible for this scenario's items. Black Cleaver Carve is 6% armor reduction per stack, max 30% (data/items.json id 3071). For a heal proportional to post-mitigation physical damage, the ratio from full Carve is (100+A)/(100+0.7A); solving = 1.4325 needs A = 456 armor, and the documented Cleaver stack-model band (0.8*max_stacks constant vs. the exact Cesaro mean C - C(C-1)/(2h), docs/math-foundations.md Sec. 2.3) moves 24% vs 30% reduction, which at A = 100 is only 176/170 = 1.035x. Cleaver cannot produce a 43% swing. Bloodsong's amp (8%/5%) cannot either, alone.
independent_computation.step_3_amp_arithmetic: Bloodsong's only combat-relevant amp is Expose Weakness: 8% (melee) / 5% (ranged) increased damage from all sources for 4s, 1.5s cooldown. The observed shift 46.7 - 32.6 = 14.1 equals exactly one 8% Expose Weakness application on 176.25 of damage (14.1 / 0.08 = 176.25), or one 5% application on 282.0. Both are ordinary per-window incoming-damage totals for one participant in a coupled roster fight. So reading (a) is quantitatively consistent with exactly ONE Expose Weakness application being removed from the damage the healed unit takes (duplicate applications merged into a single debuff factor), which fills the unit up by 14.1 and hands that 14.1 back as overheal.
independent_computation.step_4_which_direction_the_source_demand: The cached wiki text makes Expose Weakness a debuff ON THE TARGET ('inflict them with Expose Weakness for 4 seconds, causing them to take 8%/5% increased damage from all sources (1.5 second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack)'). A single named debuff on one target does not compound per applier or per re-application: one debuff instance, one factor. The engine's own documented convention for same-family modifiers is exactly this (docs/math-foundations.md Sec. 5, Grievous Wounds row: 'strongest-wins composition via min of factors; duration refresh via max ... sources do not stack (min is the game rule)'). Therefore an amp-merge that collapses duplicate Expose Weakness applications into one factor is the sourced-correct behaviour, and it strictly LOWERS the damage the healed unit takes, which strictly RAISES overheal. That is the observed direction (32.6 -> 46.7).
independent_computation.step_5_cross_check_second_mechanism: The scenario is a roster fight; the same direction falls out of a max-health correction on the healed unit. overheal = heal - (max_hp - current_hp): a downward correction of a transformed max health raises overheal one-for-one. The project's own source rule for that case (CLAUDE.md quirk note) is that Mega-form deltas must come from the game files, not the wiki stat box, which has previously OVERSTATED Mega values (5.7 AD growth claimed vs 5.5 in the game files). A game-file-sourced correction is therefore expected to move stats down, damage down, and overheal up — again the observed direction.
independent_computation.conclusion: Every mechanism I can source from the permitted evidence pushes this leaf UP when the engine is made more correct, and the exact delta (14.1) is one clean Expose Weakness application on a plausible damage total. Nothing in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md supports the old value; no sourced rule is violated by the new one.

limits_of_this_oracle: The scenario tuple for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (champions, roles, levels, ranks, fight window, roster membership) lives outside the permitted evidence tree (scripts/ and tests/ are out of bounds under R-18/R-19), so healing_events[31] cannot be resolved to a named source/actor and the health path at that timestamp cannot be replayed.

Overheal is a second-order, path-dependent quantity (heal minus missing health), not a directly sourced constant; neither data/ nor docs/math-foundations.md pins any individual event's value. The verification performed is therefore a mechanism-and-direction verification plus an exact-delta consistency check, not a bit-for-bit recomputation.

Residual risk: if healing_events[31] is a DIFFERENT event under the new engine (index shift from added/deduplicated healing events), the pair 32.6/46.7 is positional rather than semantic and both numbers could be individually correct heals. This does not change the verdict (the new snapshot is still the correct one to pin) but it would make the 'changed leaf' framing misleading; a source/time-keyed diff would settle it.

A competing arithmetic reading exists and was rejected: 32.6 = 46.7 * 0.698 is also exactly the mitigation factor 100/(100+43.25), i.e. a post-mitigation -> pre-mitigation heal-basis flip at R = 43.25. It was rejected because (a) it requires the heal to be damage-linked with an unchanged health path AND a resistance of exactly 43.25 on the damaged target, and (b) nothing in the two items under test touches heal basis. If a future receipt shows this leaf's healer is a damage-linked heal whose cached wiki text says 'post-mitigation' (Aatrox E/P, Gwen P, Morgana P, Warwick P/Q/R, Nilah, Kayn, Ambessa, Aphelios P — all POST in data/champions.json; only Vladimir W and Fiddlesticks W say PRE), the verdict must be revisited to old_value_correct.
